sections.title: Sound of dé
paragraphs: The letter name is (dé) /deː/. Its main sound is a voiced consonant that you hear in (dob) /ˈdob/, which means drum, throw. The letter has three sounds.

sections.title: How to say dé
paragraphs: For the first sound, place your tongue tip against the ridge behind your upper teeth. Stop the air for a moment, then release it with your voice on. For the second sound, make the exact same tongue movement, but turn your voice completely off. For the third sound, press the middle of your tongue flat against the roof of your mouth and release it with your voice on. Touch your throat to feel it vibrate for the voiced sounds.

sections.title: Spelling rules for dé
paragraphs: In standard positions, such as before vowels, it makes its primary sound, as in (madár) /ˈmɒdaːr/. Before voiceless consonants, assimilation turns it into a voiceless sound, heard in (adta) /ˈɒttɒ/ and (hadtest) /ˈhɒttɛʃt/. Assimilation is a change where one sound becomes more like the sound next to it. Before the letter j, it changes into a different voiced sound, heard in (adja) /ˈɒɟːɒ/.

sections.title: Mistakes to avoid with dé
paragraphs: In English words like dot, you often place the tongue further back on the gum ridge. For this Hungarian letter, place the tongue tip firmly against the teeth or right behind them. Do not keep the voice on when a voiceless consonant follows. In everyday English bad time, the first sound stays voiced, but here you must turn the voice completely off.
